baseline_requirements: Target group for the remote is people aged 15 to 35.
Remote is powered by a hybrid scheme: kinetic power with a battery as backup (the kinetic part does not charge the battery); a battery is always needed.
Battery must be good enough that users do not have to recharge or replace it every few days, given lit buttons.
Remote controls the TV only; ignore teletext and all other functions.
Functions are grouped into categories (audio-visual and other) on the remote.
Only basic functions are visible on the front; advanced, rarely used functions are hidden (e.g. inside a fold-up part).
Remote may fold up to reveal a third group of controls inside, with volume controls on the body.
Design incorporates the corporate colour and slogan.
Slogan is printed on the product, on the side of the casing.
A logo is incorporated on the device.
Yellow features in the colour scheme: yellow background with a bold contrasting colour for the buttons; possibly an all-yellow product (not confirmed).
If the corporate colour scheme allows, use a very bright colour so the remote is easy to find, avoiding tackiness.
Remote has a fancy look and feel, with style as the number one priority, appealing to the target market.
Remote is innovative in design and technology so it is seen as cutting edge, with innovation shown in look and feel rather than extra functional features (e.g. lighting up when picked up).
Remote is easy to use and user friendly throughout while still having technology.
No literal fruit-shaped remote (e.g. an apple); instead a very curvy shape with fruit-like texture and colour, observing the fruit and vegetable trend.
Use soft, spongy, ergonomic, friendly-to-handle materials, with vibrant natural colours and softness in materials, shape and function.
Possible lemon/lime theme with green and yellow colours (proposed idea, not agreed).
Avoid the hard, glassy, glossy look of the iPod; be more comfortable and friendly.
Buttons or case may light up, possibly in different colours; interchangeable covers considered.
Buttons are backlit/glowing so the remote can be found and used in the dark.
Case is slightly transparent and yellow-tinted, with one or two subtle strategically placed lights shining through for a gentle low-power glow.
Stand-by button is red for consistent user identification.
Buttons are large, easy and comfortable to press, not tiny.
Volume up and down buttons are clearly distinguishable from each other.
If voice activation is ever included, a button alternative must always exist.
No big square block look.
No talk-back or speaking function; the spoken slogan idea is dropped.
No LCD display.
Remote is comfortable to hold and sits right in the hand; small and slim but not so small it is hard to use.
Keep the number of components low and the components simple to reduce cost and time to market.
Case combines plastic with rubber on the outside for a warmer, more comfortable feel, not wood or titanium; plastic is textured to feel soft and grippy.
Snowman-type shape: a larger lower part that sits in the hand and a smaller bubble at the top for additional functions.
Buttons are rubber, flush or integrated into the case rather than standard big protruding rubber buttons.
Remote includes a jog dial for volume control, placed where it fits the device shape; possibly flat and operated by spinning. Use for channel selection is disputed.
baseline_decisions: Presentations are given in order (Andrew, Craig, David), with discussion at the end followed by decisions.
Team will find a single unifying theme or series (e.g. fruit such as lime and lemon tied to yellow) as a marketing identity to inspire shapes and keep the look coherent.
Team agreed to the snowman shape and to refer to it as the snowman-shape trademark.
Designers will work with Play-doh on shape and design before the next meeting.
The meeting must end with a decision on the product concepts; about fifteen minutes remained at one point.
Corporate colour appears to be yellow (website, bottom band); not confirmed.
Voice option unclear: supplier email said the device could talk but not listen, and mentioned an unclarified sensor.
A rubber case cannot be combined with a solar power cell.
Titanium and wooden cases cannot be curved.
LCD panel or scroll wheel requires more complicated logic, raising cost and complexity.
LCD would significantly increase cost, and there is no input device to load listings data into the remote.
Kinetic power commits users to moving the remote; infrequent users may find it a nuisance, hence the battery backup.
The next meeting is in thirty minutes.
